text:
carla: heads-up — large customer reporting duplicated processing despite Idempotency-Key. they see 429/503 spikes and the python sdk appears to immediately retry on pooled connections, ignoring jitter and sometimes dropping idempotency headers.

ben: ouch. can you paste a short repro + sdk version + logs?

carla: minimal repro below (runs against our staging proxy that returns intermittent 503 then 200). sdk==0.10.0, python 3.10, requests 2.31.0, urllib3 2.0.6.
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
for i in range(3):
    try:
        r = client.text_generate("hello world")
        print('ok', r.status_code)
    except Exception as e:
        print('err', e)
```

logs (truncated):
[2026-03-10 15:11:01] DEBUG retry=0 sending request id=abc123 headers={'Idempotency-Key': 'abc123'}
[2026-03-10 15:11:01] DEBUG recv 503 id=abc123
[2026-03-10 15:11:01] DEBUG retry=1 sending request id=abc123 headers={}   <-- sometimes header missing
[2026-03-10 15:11:01] DEBUG recv 429 id=abc123
[2026-03-10 15:11:01] DEBUG retry=2 sending request id=abc123 headers={}   <-- immediate retry, no backoff
```

rachel: that looks like two things: (1) idempotency header not preserved on connection reuse, (2) backoff/jitter not applied (or computed as 0). any chance you can repro with pool_size=1 so reuse happens every time? also does pinning to 0.9.x avoid it?

carla: yes — forcing pool_maxsize=1 makes it reproduce 100% locally. pinned to 0.9.4 and problem goes away.

ben: thanks. can you confirm if this is only when keep-alive reuse happens? and whether it's sync vs async client?

carla: sync client (requests-backed). when connection is fresh, idempotency header is present. when reused, second attempt sometimes loses header. backoff delay logged as 0.0ms for retry=1.

infra: tagging eng-runtime. fyi: we recently changed our retry state object to be stored on the connection pool entry to reuse across attempts — might be related.

sdk-bot: Created issue RW-5043: "python-sdk: idempotency header dropped + jitter zero on pooled connection retries" — assigned to eng-runtime. ticket: https://tracker.redwood/issue/RW-5043

rachel: next steps: (a) eng-runtime to triage RW-5043 and add unit test that simulates pooled connection + transient 503/429, (b) support to recommend workaround (pin sdk to 0.9.4 or set env var REDWOOD_RETRY_DISABLE_POOL_REUSE=true if using staging), (c) get capture of full request/response (headers) from affected customer.

ben: also ask customer to attach SDK debug log (REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug) and their requests/urllib3 versions. will open escalation ticket if they are on latest deps.

carla: I've got logs from customer — uploaded to the ticket. they are on requests 2.31 and urllib3 2.0.6.

rachel: putting a P0 on eng-runtime to investigate. possible quick fix: ensure retry state is copied per-request (not mutated on pool reuse) and preserve headers when reissuing on same logical request. also check jitter RNG seeding; looks like seed may be reinitialized to 0 on connection reuse which yields no jitter.

infra: adding a canary rollout for the fix once merged, and we'll add a small synthetic test that hits staging proxy with deterministic 503->429 to assert header preservation + nonzero backoff.

carla: thanks — customer notified about workaround (pin to 0.9.4) and we've offered a temporary SLA credit if this caused duplicate billing.

ben: assign to @rachel for follow-up and update on RW-5043. i'll coordinate with support to send repro steps to the customer's infra team.

rachel: will take it. expected timeline: reproduce + PR in 48h, canary next deploy after review.

carla: great, keeping this thread posted with any new customer info. :thumbsup:
